claim: An input trace replays any run bit-identically
why: test/test_trace.jl:543 asserts that replay reproduces the recorded trajectory bitwise. The probe recorded a staged, localized-event run and replayed it on a twin whose condition differed. P007 gives bit-identical true at RK4, and true under an adaptive BS3 deployment.

claim: The bit-for-bit replay promise holds only against the identical build running identical compiled code
why: Replay re-runs the ordinary loop (src/sim.jl:1281-1283: the replayed prefix is bit-identical). The header checks (CheckpointMismatch and ReplaySchemaMismatch, src/sim.jl:1310-1313 in the docstring) refuse a mismatched model but cannot certify the compiled code. Nothing in the code extends the promise beyond identical code, so the limit the doc states holds.

claim: The same build compiled at another optimization level agrees only to round-off
why: Probe P3, run at -O2 and at -O0 (P1 prints opt_level 2 and 0): the Bouncer final q bits agree on this small model. That does not contradict the claim, which only bounds agreement at round-off. No src code promises bit identity across optimization levels, and spec §9.7 (spec:6302-6305) states the same bound. | Bit identity on one small model is consistent with the claim, which allows round-off differences but does not require them.

claim: Each continuous state leaf is a real scalar or an SArray
why: src/assembly.jl:672-682 `check_state_leaves` admits each x_init field, or a bare value, only when it is a Float64 or an SArray of Float64, and refuses anything else as IllegalStateLeaf. | The code also requires the common eltype (Float64 at declaration), which §7.1 states and this summary line leaves out. A Float32 scalar is refused as :eltype. The line is consistent with §7.1's 'plain real scalars and SArrays of a common eltype'.

claim: Each field-emitting component also exposes a value-level constructor, a plain public function from its input values to its handle.
why: src/library.jl ships no field-emitting component (rg finds no handle-typed `y_types` there), so no shipped component lacks the constructor. The suite's one field emitter carries it: test/fixtures.jl:1429 `height_field(c::Terrain) = HeightField(c.z, c.h0)`, and its stage calls it at test/fixtures.jl:1433. | This is an author's obligation the code cannot enforce. It holds wherever a field emitter exists in the tree.
